item.title: Weekly Newsletter #39 — August 19, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #39 · August 19, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🎫 CITYNERD LIVE IN PHILLY

🚌 TONIGHT: STATEWIDE TRANSIT FUNDING CALL

Transit agencies across PA have already had to make severe cuts and implement large fare hikes--we're next in 2027 if we don't find a new source of transit funding.

🚲 IMPROVE BIKING IN YOUR NEIGHBORHOOD

Philly Bike Action is launching a Community Action fund to provide financial support for projects that create tangible improvements for people biking in Philadelphia.
Applicants can  for a grant of $250-2,000.
They're looking for proposals like:
  • Bike racks or bike parking
  • Community bike repair or maintenance events
  • Bike lights, helmets, or other safety equipment for community distribution
  • Traffic calming or safety improvements (with appropriate approvals)

🪑 PEDESTRIANIZED SOUTH STREET

The event will feature live music, food, and a movie.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes! And use this tool for a quick form letter to contact your representatives.

📅 EVENTS

Aug 19

DVRPC Annual Work Program Workshop

5:30 to 7:30 PM · DVRPC Office (190 N Independence Mall W), or Virtual

Attend this DVRPC workshop to share feedback on proposed transportation planning projects. The DVRPC makes important planning decisions for the region--this is a great opportunity to advocate for further bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure.
Aug 19

Transit for All PA Statewide All-Call

6:00 to 7:00 PM · Virtual

Join Transit for All PA for a statewide call covering the 2026-2027 state budget and the clauses within it that give transit riders an opening to win next year.
Aug 27

Transit Forward Philly Book Club: When Driving Is Not an Option

5:30 to 7:00 PM · 2717 Aramingo Ave

Join Transit Forward Philly's next book club, covering Anna Zivarts' When Driving Is Not an Option.
Aug 29, 30

Bring Your Own Chair South Street

4:00 to 10:00 PM · South Street between 2nd and 4th Streets

South Street goes car free for the weekend, featuring live music, food, and a movie.
Sep 27

Route 13 Advocacy Walk

10:00 AM to 6:00 PM · Hunting Park

Between 2019 and 2023, Route 13 has seen 123 fatal and serious injury crashes--it's time for a change. Advocates, friends and families of victims of traffic violence are walking Route 13 to raise awareness about the need for speed cameras to reduce crashes and saves lives.
Oct 29

Pitchfest: Transportation

2:30 to 6:30 PM · Penn Museum, Widener Lecture Hall, 3260 South St

Transportation Initiative at Penn is hosting an event designed to connect transportation-focused public agencies with faculty and staff at the University of Pennsylvania to collaborate on applied research projects. Public agency staff are invited to give low-stakes, two-minute pitches on short-term, high-impact projects that could benefit from external expert support.

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

Inquirer.com / Site of the Walnut Street Beer Garden will become a two-story retail building, not an apartment tower

Inquirer.com / Millennial homeownership in the Philly area almost doubled in 5 years, outpacing every other major Northeastern metro

Inquirer.com / 45 affordable apartments for artists on Broad Street will be partly funded by Knight Foundation

Inquirer.com / New York developer proposes 129 affordable apartments near Temple University

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

Inquirer.com / Philly’s new Broad St. planters turn what could be a grand avenue into a highway | Opinion

🚌 TRANSIT

PhillyVoice / SEPTA to add new bus routes and remove lesser-used ones starting Sunday

🚲 MOBILITY

Inquirer.com / Self-policing loading zones have worked in Center City, the PPA says, so they’re adding more

💼 JOB OPPORTUNITIES

Bicycle Coalition of Greater Philadelphia / Operations Coordinator

SEPTA

  • Front-End Software Engineer
  • Assistant General Manager of Revenue Development
  • Bus Operator / Light Rail Operator, City
  • Marketing Coordinator

City of Philadelphia

  • Workforce Development Manager - Transportation and Infrastructure
  • Legislative Planning Intern - Planning and Development
  • Citizens Planning Institute Intern
  • Planning and Development - Communications Intern
  • Comp Plan Intern

Fair Share Housing Center / Managing Director of Policy & Advocacy

Printfresh / Real Estate Manager

PBA / (Grant) Community Action Fund

10,000 Friends of PA / Fundraising and Communications Manager

DVRPC

  • Infrastructure Financing Coordinator
  • Smart Growth Intern

Southwest CDC / Community Engagement Specialist

Office of State Rep Sierra McNeil / Resume Bank

New Kensington Community Development Corporation

  • TCB Corridor Manager
  • TCB Corridor Coordinator

Econsult

  • Analyst
  • Senior Analyst

Hexagon Studio Architects / Architectural Designer

Accelerator for America

  • Housing Project Director
  • Housing Program Manager
  • Housing Policy and Program Analyst

Office of Councilmember Gauthier / Interns

The Common Wheel / Executive Director

Chamber of Commerce for Greater Philadelphia / Manager, Business Attraction & Expansion

Committee of Seventy / Senior Director of External Affairs

NV5

  • Transportation Engineer

  • Transportation Project Manager

 

Do You Like This Newsletter and Our Advocacy Work?

We need your support to sustain Philly's Urbanist Movement — and you get cool perks too.

Join Us as a Member TODAY

 

5th Square Advocacy is a grassroots nonprofit organization driven to advance a vision for a more accessible, sustainable, equitable Philadelphia for all residents. Donations are not tax deductible.

Website Instagram Become a Member Volunteer

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #38 — August 12, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #38 · August 12, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🕯️ FRIDAY: REMEMBERING GLENN COLVILLE JR.

 

📣 MARKET EAST ENGAGEMENT

The Philadelphia Department of Planning & Development is seeking input and is holding an after-hours community night at their pop-up storefront.

After Hours Community Night
This Wednesday, August 12th, 6-8pm
My Market East Engagement Hub, 930 Market St

"My Market East" is a City-operated storefront where you can drop in and learn about the Market East Revival and share your vision for the future of Market East.

Can't make the event? The hub will be open every Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday from 12-6pm through August 28th.

You can also read more and give input via online survey here.

🚶 SUPPORT PEDESTRIAN AND BIKE INFRASTRUCTURE

Attend the Delaware Valley Regional Planning Commission’s workshop on August 19th at 6pm to share feedback on proposed transportation planning projects.

The DVRPC makes important planning decisions for the region--this is a great opportunity to advocate for further bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure!

In-person and Zoom access offered. Dinner provided in-person. Register here.

📆 CITY NERD IS COMING TO PHILLY

🗞️ 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Philadelphia Tribune / What to know about SEPTA's new routes, service cuts and schedule changes beginning Aug. 23
Transit advocates who have followed the redesign process say the first phase is less dramatic than earlier proposals that generated significant public concern.
“This phase is not going to be as disruptive,” said Jerrett Johnson, lead transit organizer and board member of the advocacy group 5th Square.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes! And use this tool for a quick form letter to contact your representatives.

Aug 11

5:00 to 7:00 PM · CreativePHL Office, City Hall Room 116

Join Transit Forward Philly and Art-Reach to audit bus stop conditions in Center City near arts destinations.
Aug 12

Market East After Hours Community Night

6:00 to 8:00 PM · My Market East Engagement Hub, 930 Market St

Tell the city you want to see safer streets, protected bike lanes, better transit access, dense housing, and mixed-use development along Market East! The Philadelphia Department of Planning & Development is seeking input and is holding an after-hours community night at their pop-up storefront.
Aug 14

Glenn Colville Jr. Memorial Ride & Ghost Bike Dedication

7:00 PM · 2717 Aramingo Ave

Join Glenn's loved ones at Aramingo and Lehigh Ave where Glenn Colville Jr. was tragically killed by traffic violence for a 7.5 mile ride in Glenn’s memory and a Ghost Bike installation ceremony.
Aug 27

Transit Forward Philly Book Club: When Driving Is Not an Option

5:30 to 7:00 PM · 2717 Aramingo Ave

Oct 29

2:30 to 6:30 PM · Penn Museum, Widener Lecture Hall, 3260 South St

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #36 — August 5, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #36 · August 05, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📆 CITY NERD IS COMING TO PHILLY

💰🚲 BIKE IMPROVEMENT GRANTS

🎨 ARTS ACCESSIBILITY AUDIT

🚲 PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes make our streets safer for all road users, but they're not allowed on state roads--help us change that!
For years, the Bicycle Coalition has been leading the charge to legalize parking-protected bike lanes in PA. Let's make it happen this year!
We need you to contact your legislators and ask them to support HB 291.
Use this tool for a quick form letter and contact information for your representatives. It only takes two minutes!

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #35 — July 21, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #35 · July 21, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📢 FRIDAY: RALLY FOR A SAFER WEST MARKET STREET

🌉 DELAWARE RIVER BRIDGE BIKE/PED PATH

Tell the Turnpike Commission that we need a shared-use path on their new bridge over the Delaware River!

There is currently zero bike/pedestrian access over the Delaware River between Philadelphia and Trenton, a 25 mile gap.

The replacement of the I-95 bridge over the Delaware gives us a rare opportunity to shrink this gap and substantially improve connections between neighborhoods in PA and NJ.

Submit your comment here!

🚌 ANOTHER BUDGET WITHOUT TRANSIT FUNDING

Last week, Harrisburg passed another budget without any new revenue for public transit, setting SEPTA up for catastrophic cuts in 2027.

But we can still stop this! Contact your legislators to remind them that they can't forget about transit!

🌻 REMEMBERING DR. BARBARA FRIEDES

This past Sunday, there was a touching memorial for Dr. Barbara Friedes, two years after she was killed while biking on Spruce Street by a reckless driver.
Check out this video if you weren't able to make it.
During the memorial, Council President Kenyatta Johnson expressed his support for concrete bike lane protection, and attendees poured water into a symbolic jersey barrier.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #34 — July 14, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #34 · July 14, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🕯️ SUNDAY: MEMORIAL FOR DR. BARBARA FRIEDES

This Sunday, join us for a community memorial event to remember the life and legacy of Dr. Barbara Friedes.
We'll meet at 8:30 AM at Barbara's Angel Bike at 18th and Spruce. Please bring a filled reusable water to pour into a symbolic memorial.

🎉 A FEDERAL HOUSING WIN

Good news! The bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act is now law!
Though it's not a perfect piece of legislation, it includes important provisions for boosting housing construction and it's a sign that Congress is beginning to take the housing crisis seriously.
Read more in this piece from the Niskanen Center: 3 reasons the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act matters

🍻 HOUSING HAPPY HOUR RECAP

Thank you to everyone who came out to our Housing Happy Hour last week!
We had a great time discussing our ongoing campaigns, including our efforts to fight for more homes near transit, ADU legalization legislation, and a "Golden Girls Law".

🚇 SATURDAY: TRANSPORTATIONCAMP PHL

TransportationCamp PHL's Summer Gathering is this Saturday!
Transportation professionals, students, and advocates will get together for a free "unconference" gathering, featuring fun social activities.
Join them at 11:30 AM at 30th Street Station for the kickoff.
 

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

Inside Climate News / Pennsylvania’s Legislature Is Likely to Punt on Mass Transit Funding—Again

“There is no excuse left for lawmakers. In the year we celebrate 250 years of this great country, let’s fund the system that moves it, and let’s get it done by June 30,” said Dr. Jay Arzu of 5th Square Advocacy, an urbanist group, at the rally. 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

👂 TELL US ABOUT YOUR RCO

Are you involved in your local RCO? Fill out this quick form with which RCO you're a part of and what your role is.

  

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

 

🏫 UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES PETITION

Sign this petition to support expanding student transit cards to cover more students and provide transit access on evenings, weekends, and summers.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

Join transportation professionals, students, and advocates for a free "unconference" gathering, featuring fun social activities.

Join us in remembering the life of Dr. Barbara Friedes with a community memorial event. Please bring a full reusable water bottle to pour into the symbolic memorial.

3:00 PM to 5:00PM · PHA Headquarters, 2013 Ridge Ave

Small developers, bring your W-9s and MBE/WBE-certifications and get registered with PHA on the spot.

Join us to demand PennDOT implement the safety improvements we called for alongside PBA in our joint West Market St petition. We'll join elected officials in speaking out about the urgent need to implement these changes. Bring your safe streets signs for the media to see!

item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #32 · July 02, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🏘️ INSIDE OUR CAMPAIGN FOR MORE HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Check out Tuesday’s episode of the City Cast Philly podcast featuring our board member Fae Ehsan in a deep dive into our More Homes Near Transit campaign!

👂 TELL US ABOUT YOUR RCO

Are you involved in your local RCO?

If you are, we want to know! Fill out this quick form with which RCO you're a part of and what your role is.

Don't know what an RCO is? Read this for an explainer and find your RCO here. RCOs play important roles in approving housing and safe streets projects--they're a great way to get directly involved in making your neighborhood a better place to live.

🎉 EXPANDED MARKET ST REDESIGN

Ever since it officially opened last month, we've been huge fans of the newly redesigned Market Street between 2nd and 6th Streets. The freshly installed traffic calming and protected bike lanes make the street much safer and more pleasant to use.

And now, this redesign is headed all the way to City Hall!

The City recently received a $2.5 million federal grant to begin planning work for the portion of Market between 6th and City Hall, and we can't wait to see their new designs.

Check out Tuesday’s episode of the City Cast Philly podcast featuring our board member Fae Ehsan in a deep dive into our More Homes Near Transit campaign!

👂 TELL US ABOUT YOUR RCO

Are you involved in your local RCO?

If you are, we want to know! Fill out this quick form with which RCO you're a part of and what your role is.

Don't know what an RCO is? Read this for an explainer and find your RCO here. RCOs play important roles in approving housing and safe streets projects--they're a great way to get directly involved in making your neighborhood a better place to live.

🎉 EXPANDED MARKET ST REDESIGN

Ever since it officially opened last month, we've been huge fans of the newly redesigned Market Street between 2nd and 6th Streets. The freshly installed traffic calming and protected bike lanes make the street much safer and more pleasant to use.

And now, this redesign is headed all the way to City Hall!

The City recently received a $2.5 million federal grant to begin planning work for the portion of Market between 6th and City Hall, and we can't wait to see their new designs.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #31 — June 25, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #31 · June 25, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📢 FRIDAY: RALLY FOR TRANSIT FUNDING

Pennsylvania needs new revenue sources to keep transit systems moving across the Commonwealth. At this critical moment, transit supporters can take action now to encourage their legislators to create new revenue sources that keep transit moving in every PA community.

Join us this Friday, June 26th, at 10am at the 5th St./Independence Hall L stop for a rally and press conference calling on Harrisburg to fund public transit!

Almost every transit agency across the state is making cuts due to a lack of state funding--we need your help to stop this!

How else can you help?

  1. Sign and share this take action link from our friends at Transit For All PA. It's quick and easy, takes less than two minutes!
  2. Sign up to make a few calls to your legislators on your lunch hour this Thursday.

🚲👶 BIKING WITH TODDLERS

Want to bike with your baby, toddler, or young child, but unsure how to do it safely?

Join Philly Bike Action's Biking with Toddlers 101 Webinar this Saturday! The webinar will feature a presentation by two local doctors, followed by a Q&A section.

📈 WHY PEDESTRIAN DEATHS ARE RISING

Despite drops in pedestrian fatalities in peer countries across the world, US pedestrian deaths are up substantially over the past two decades.

Why is the US falling behind? At least part of the answer is our giant trucks and SUVs.

This piece from the New York Times does a great job visualizing how larger vehicles pose a much greater danger to pedestrians on our streets. From larger blind spots, to higher hood heights, crashes are both more likely and more deadly.

The New York Times: The Deadly Rise of Giant Trucks and S.U.V.s

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Philadelphia Citizen / Guest Commentary: Seeking Someone to Volun-tell our Volunteers

Last weekend, the crown jewel FDR playground’s water fountains were broken and there was broken fencing all around it, a symptom of its haphazard closure due to safety concerns. 5th Square’s Will Tung noted in City Council that after a $27 million Rebuild renovation, Kingessing Rec Center suffered a plumbing failure that destroyed its brand-new basketball court.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

 

🏫 UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES PETITION

Sign this petition to support expanding student transit cards to cover more students and provide transit access on evenings, weekends, and summers.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

📅 EVENTS

Jun 25

Fund Transit Lunch Hour - Call your Elected Officials!

12:00 PM to 1:00 PM · Online via Zoom

Join Transit Forward Philadelphia, Transit For All PA, and partners to make phone calls to your State Representative, State Senator, and Governor Shapiro to fund transit.
Jun 25

Transit Forward Philly Book Club: Life After Cars

5:30 PM · 1500 Walnut St, 8th Floor

Join Transit Forward Philadelphia for a book club discussion of Life After Cars.
Jun 27

Bagel Day Transit Tour

10:00 AM · Marconi Plaza, meet at Guglielmo Marconi statue

Transit Forward Philly will be hosting a Transit Tour to get bagels in Brewerytown. Join them if you are new to riding SEPTA or just want to ride transit together.
Jun 27

Biking with Toddlers 101 Webinar

1:30 PM to 2:30 PM · Online Webinar

Learn how to safely bike with young children. This webinar will feature a presentation by two local doctors followed by a Q&A section.
Jun 28

Teddy Einstein Exit Party

2:00 PM to 8:00 PM · Clark Park

Celebrate the life of Teddy Einstein with life stations commemorating the different chapters of his life amidst food, drinks, and lawn games.
Jun 30

5:30 PM to 8:00 PM · TFP Office, 1500 Walnut St, Ste 1507

Transit Forward Philly is launching a campaign to audit the top 100 most used bus stops in Philly. It will be kicked off with water ice, audit training, and joining a team to complete as many audits as possible in the time frame.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #30 — June 17, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #30 · June 17, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🥳 COUNCIL PASSED TOC BILL

This past week, City Council passed the Transit-Oriented Communities bill which aims to boost housing development within a quarter mile of select transit stations.

🗓️ NEXT MONTH: TRANSPORTATIONCAMP PHL

🏛️ TONIGHT: POLICY SOCIAL/CELEBRATION

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🗞️ 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Inquirer: Philly has a new law to boost development around transit. Which neighborhoods will benefit?

The urbanist group 5th Square had been meeting with City Council members in advance of Thursday’s final vote on the bill strengthening transit-oriented development.
...
“The idea that all of the stations will be opted in at once is unlikely,” said Jay Arzu, housing organizer with 5th Square and the founder of the Roosevelt Boulevard Subway Movement.

“They made the intention clear that they’ll look at it on an individual, case-by-case basis, which is disappointing for transit advocates,” Arzu said. “But we recognize it’s another step in the right direction. Sometimes you just got to take what you can get.”

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏘️🚇 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Sign to show your support for more homes near transit! City Council passed a bill to increase housing near certain transit stations--we need your support to expand coverage to additional stations citywide.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #29 — June 10, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #29 · June 10, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🏛️ WE WENT TO HARRISBURG

Yesterday, we went to Harrisburg with the Bicycle Coalition, PA Safe Roads PAC, and Families for Safe Streets to show our support for safer streets for all.

🏘️ HOMES BELONG NEAR TRANSIT

Support more homes near transit!

Our city's vast transit network is an incredible asset--but restrictive zoning around transit stops prevents us from taking full advantage of it!

Homes near frequent transit provide valuable access to car-free transportation, but the areas around our transit stations are far too often filled with parking lots and drive-thrus.

Bill 260517 is a step in the right direction towards fixing this, but it only applies to 13 stations on the L.

City Council needs to pass this bill and follow it up with additional legislation adding stations on the B, T, Regional Rail, and our busiest bus corridors.

Read more in this piece in the Inquirer from our housing organizer, Jay Arzu: Philadelphia built a mass transit system. Now let people live next to it. | Opinion

🛠️ THE FIX FOR MORE PUBLIC SPACES

We love Philadelphia's public spaces.

But there's a little known barrier working against them: insurance costs.

The City requires that stewards of public spaces--parklets, streeteries, pedestrian plazas--hold insurance, and that they indemnify the city in the event of lawsuits.

This has high costs, and the evidence suggests it's not even needed!

Read more in the Philadelphia Citizen: Guest Commentary: The Insurance Trap Killing Our Public Spaces

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🗞️ 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

Inquirer.com / Philadelphia built a mass transit system. Now let people live next to it. | Opinion

The bill covers just 13 stations, all on the Market-Frankford Line. Most Philadelphians do not live near the El. I think about the family in the Northeast that cannot reach a steady job without a second car. I think about the retiree near Broad Street who cannot easily get to one of our region’s best hospitals. If the zoning change stops there, we will have passed a good policy and confined it to a footprint too small to reach them.

–5th Square Advocacy Housing Organizer Jay Arzu

The Philadelphia Citizen / Guest Commentary: A Dollar Won’t Do

The Mayor and City Council should reject the flat fee, accept the percentage-based structure, and advocate for a rate high enough to actually matter. The reason to get this right goes beyond this year’s school budget. Philadelphia, and every other American city, has a narrow window to establish sound rideshare tax policy before widespread autonomous vehicles make it politically much harder.

–5th Square Advocacy Treasurer Russell Richie

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏫 UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES PETITION

Sign this petition to support expanding student transit cards to cover more students and provide transit access on evenings, weekends, and summers.

 

✍️ TRAIL SURVEY

Take this quick, 3-minute survey to help the Bicycle Coalition and Circuit Trails understand how you use trails throughout the region.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

📅 EVENTS

Jun 11

SW Philly Transit Accessibility Audit

5:00 PM to 7:00 PM · Cobbs Creek Library, 5800 Cobbs Creek Parkway

Join Transit Forward Philly for an accessibility audit of bus and trolley stops in SW Philly.
Jun 17

Policy Social and Celebration with BCGP and TFP

5:30 PM · Resurrection Philadelphia, 123 S 17th St

Join the Bicycle Coalition and Transit Forward Philly to celebrate wins in bike advocacy, Circuit Trails, transit, and pedestrian safety! BCGP Policy Director Julio Rodriguez will share policy priorities for 2026, and attendees will discuss ideas for the coming year.
Jun 27

Biking with Toddlers 101 Webinar

1:30 PM to 2:30 PM · Online Webinar

Learn how to safely bike with young children. This webinar will feature a presentation by two local doctors followed by a Q&A section.
Jun 28

Teddy Einstein Exit Party

2:00 PM to 8:00 PM · Clark Park

Celebrate the life of Teddy Einstein with life stations commemorating the different chapters of his life amidst food, drinks, and lawn games.
Aug 08

Philly Mayor's Cup

Belmont Plateau

The Philly Running Alliance is hosting a team race where runners compete for their chosen local running club, featuring races of varying length through historic West Fairmount Park.

 

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #28 — June 2, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #28 · June 02, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🌇 TUESDAY OPEN STREETS

For the month of June, Center City District is bringing open streets to the Gayborhood on Tuesdays from 4:00-9:00 PM--and the first one is today!

 

🚲 ARAMINGO AVE SAFETY UPGRADES

We recently asked for your help in calling on PennDOT to make Aramingo Ave safer following the death of Glen Colville at the hands of a driver who plowed through flex posts into the bike lane.

At a meeting last week, PennDOT announced that it will replace flexposts with Toronto-style concrete barriers. While we wish it was done sooner, it's a great change that will hopefully prevent more families from losing loved ones.

Source: PBA

Thank you for signing the petition and thank you our partners at the Bicycle Coalition and PBA for supporting a safer Aramingo Ave.

💳 PUSH FOR UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES BEFORE SUMMER

🏟️ THE SPORTS COMPLEX NEEDS MORE TRANSIT

At a time when SEPTA is still facing a long-term funding crisis, last week's announcement from Gov. Shapiro of $30 million in state funds for Stadium District roadways was a major disappointment.

The best way to reduce congestion is by investing in transit, not more road capacity. We need the support of the Commonwealth to make that happen.

See our full statement here.

👶 BIKING WITH TODDLERS

Our streets are for everyone and that includes toddlers!

Want to try biking with your young child, but unsure how to do it safely?

Join Philly Bike Action's webinar on June 27th. This one-hour webinar will discuss strategies for biking safely with young children, featuring a presentation by local doctors, and a Q&A section at the end. 

🔍 TRANSIT ACCESSIBILITY AUDIT

This Saturday, June 6th, join Transit Forward Philly for an accessibility audit of bus and L stops in Kensington.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🗞️ 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Inquirer / Gov. Shapiro announces almost $30 million highway investment for Philly stadium district

“Today’s announcement from Gov. Shapiro spending $30 million in state funds for Stadium District roadways is a major disappointment when SEPTA is still facing a long-term funding crisis threatening transit service,” transit advocacy group Fifth Square said in a statement Thursday. “The most effective way to manage congestion at the Stadium District is to encourage spectators to take SEPTA instead.”

Metro Philadelphia / Philly rolls out traffic safety signs amid string of deadly crashes

“In a collision at 25 miles per hour, pedestrians have a 90% chance of surviving,” Miles Owen, of 5th Square, said at a news conference Monday morning. “That percentage drastically decreases as the speed goes up. This sign makes that visible and reinforces the stakes.”

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏫 UNIVERSAL STUDENT FARES PETITION

Sign this petition to support expanding student transit cards to cover more students and provide transit access on evenings, weekends, and summers.

 

✍️ TRAIL SURVEY

Take this quick, 3-minute survey to help the Bicycle Coalition and Circuit Trails understand how you use trails throughout the region.

 

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

📅 EVENTS

Jun 03

Transit for All PA Harrisburg Day of Action

9:30 AM to 3:30 PM · PA Capitol Building / Travel from 30th St Station

Transit systems all across the Commonwealth are facing dire funding shortfalls--join transit riders and workers from across PA in Harrisburg to demand action from our legislators.
Jun 04

Statewide Active Transportation Summit

8:30 AM to 4:30 PM · Harrisburg: 212 Locust St

Pennsylvanians from across the state working on improving walking, biking, and accessibility will gather in Harrisburg to meet others doing this work in their communities, see examples of work underway, and discover key elements to help you bring active transportation improvements home for your area.
Jun 06

Belmont Water Treatment Plant Open House

10:00 AM to 2:00 PM · Belmont Water Treatment Plant, 4300 W Ford Rd

The Philadelphia Water Department is welcoming the public for tours of a drinking water treatment plant. Come see how PWD keeps your tap water safe to drink and use every day.
Jun 06

Kensington Transit Accessibility Audit

11:00 AM to 1:00 PM · Harrowgate Park, 3455 Kensington Ave

Join Transit Forward Philadelphia for accessibility audit of bus and L stops in Kensington.
Jun 09

Bridging Blocks | Streets for Everyone: Bikes, Cars, and Pedestrian Rights

5:30 PM to 7:30 PM · Parkway Central Library, 4FL Skyline Room

Join WHYY for a community conversation discussing the safety of people walking and biking in Philadelphia and what city leaders, decision-makers, and advocates can do to improve safety.
Jun 27

Biking with Toddlers 101 Webinar

1:30 PM to 2:30 PM · Online Webinar

Learn how to safely bike with young children. This webinar will feature a presentation by two local doctors followed by a Q&A section.
Aug 08

Philly Mayor's Cup

Belmont Plateau

The Philly Running Alliance is hosting a team race where runners compete for their chosen local running club, featuring races of varying length through historic West Fairmount Park.

 

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #27 — May 26, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #27 · May 26, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🏘️ MORE HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Help us push for more homes near transit!

Philadelphia faces interconnected crises: rising housing costs, skyrocketing gas prices, worsening traffic, and a SEPTA budget shortfall. There's a $0 solution — Transit-Oriented Communities (TOC) legislation.

Mayor Parker's proposed TOC bills would allow more housing near transit, boosting SEPTA ridership and helping more residents put down roots in the city.

However the current legislation falls short: only 13 L stations are included (0 B stations!), and parking mandates near transit remain in place.

Support stronger legislation with:

  • Full removal of parking mandates near transit
  • Coverage expanded to the Broad Street Line, Regional Rail, and trolleys
  • A ½-mile radius around each transit stop
  • By-right multifamily housing in residential districts near transit

🕯️ RESCHEDULED: RIDE OF SILENCE TOMORROW

Due to last Wednesday's heavy rain, the annual Ride of Silence has been rescheduled for tomorrow, Wednesday, May 27th.

To honor the bicyclists killed or injured on our streets over the past year, we'll ride together in complete silence.

The ride will leave from City Hall, traveling 8 miles at a slow, casual pace to the Art Museum for a brief memorial bike lift.

2026 Ride of Silence
RESCHEDULED: Tomorrow, Wednesday, May 27th, 6:45 PM
North Apron of City Hall to Art Museum Steps

📣 SUPPORT THE CIRCUIT TRAILS

The Circuit Trails needs your help!

Under the current presidential administration, federal funding for bicycle and pedestrian infrastructure is rapidly drying up.

You can help by sending a letter to officials, asking them to support continued investment, maintenance and expansion of the Circuit trails across the region to ensure they remain safe and accessible for all.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🗞️ 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Philadelphia Tribune / Opposition builds against school district's fare evasion program

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🏘️ MORE HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Help us push for more homes near transit!

Philadelphia faces interconnected crises: rising housing costs, skyrocketing gas prices, worsening traffic, and a SEPTA budget shortfall. There's a $0 solution — Transit-Oriented Communities (TOC) legislation.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #25 — May 13, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #25 · May 13, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📚 TOMORROW: LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

It's finally here: our book talk event with Life After Cars authors Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon is tomorrow night!

Life After Cars Book Event
with Sarah Goodyear & Doug Gordon from The War on Cars Podcast
TOMORROW, THURSDAY, May 14th at 7 PM
Resurrection Philadelphia, 17th & Sansom Streets

Get Your Ticket Today

 
The event will be kicked off by safe-streets champion, State Senator Nikil Saval, with Inquirer architecture critic Inga Saffron as emcee. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.

Get Your Ticket Today

🕯️ RIDE OF SILENCE NEXT WEEK

Next week on Wednesday, May 20th, join us for the Ride of Silence.

To honor the bicyclists killed or injured on our streets over the past year, we'll ride together in complete silence.

The ride will leave from City Hall, traveling 8 miles at a slow, casual pace to the Art Museum for a brief memorial bike lift.

2026 Ride of Silence
Wednesday, May 20th, 6:45 PM
North Apron of City Hall to Art Museum Steps

🚘 SAFER STREETS... FOR DRIVERS

Our streets are getting safer... for some road users.

An analysis by Philly Bike Action found that while overall fatal crashes decreased last year, crashes with serious injuries were up for non-motorists! This means more pedestrians and micromobility riders were getting hit and seriously injured by drivers.

Any reduction in deaths on our streets is a step in the right direction, but we can't leave vulnerable road users behind. We need streets that are safe for all, not just those behind the wheel.

Here are three actions you can take to help make that happen:

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🏛️ SUPPORT A BUDGET THAT KEEPS PHILLY MOVING

Next Wednesday at 10am, come to City Hall to speak in support of our transportation budget priorities.

FY27 City Council Budget Hearings - Public Comment
Philadelphia City Council Chambers, City Hall, Room 400
Wednesday, May 6th, 10am

See here for more details about how to sign up, and resources to help you craft your testimony.

You can also help by taking City Council's city budget survey.

📚 TWO WEEKS: LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

Get your tickets before they sell out!

Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM — Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. The event will be kicked off by safe-streets champion Senator Nikil Saval, with Inquirer architecture critic Inga Saffron as emcee. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.
 
Get Your Ticket Today

🚏 NEW BUS TERMINAL NOW OPEN

We were thrilled to attend the opening of the newly-renovated intercity bus terminal! After years of advocacy working with Transit Forward Philadelphia, we celebrate the city finally treating bus riders with dignity.

🏫 STUDENTS DESERVE BETTER TRANSIT ACCESS

Current student fare cards don't do enough to meet the needs of Philadelphia's students--sign this petition to give them the transit access they deserve!

We need students fare cards that expand coverage to evenings, weekends, and summers, and are given to all students regardless of where in the city they live.

🚲 $1 INDEGO PASSES

To celebrate Bike Month, Indego is offering $1 monthly passes with promo code INDEPRO26.

✍️ TRAIL SURVEY

The Bicycle Coalition and Circuit Trails want to know your thoughts about trails in the Greater Philadelphia and southern New Jersey region and how you use them.

Take their quick, 3-minute survey here!

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

Billy Penn at WHYY / Philadelphia aims to expand delivery loading zones

“Just the past few years, e-commerce and food-ordering businesses have exploded in popularity and caused tremendous stress in our roads and along our curbs,” testified Miles Owen, co-chair of the 5th Square Advocacy urbanist group. “These bills are absolutely necessary and smart policy to modernize the use of curb space in our city to make roads safer.”

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

📅 EVENTS

Apr 30

Parking Protected Bike Lane & Pedestrian Safety Advocacy Call

6:00 PM to 7:00 PM · Virtual via Zoom

Join Bicycle Coalition Policy Director Julio Rodriguez for a virtual call about Parking Protected Bike Lanes (PPB), Jay Alert Pilot, Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA), and their upcoming June 9 advocacy day in Harrisburg.
May 02

John Heinz Bike Tour

2:00 PM to 3:00 PM · John Heinz National Wildlife Refuge

Join Ranger Ben for a Bike Tour around John Heinz NWR! Bring your own bike for this 4-5 mile ride on gravel trails. Register with Ben at benjamin_breslau@fws.gov.
May 14

Life After Cars Book Talk

7:00 PM, doors open 6:30 PM · Resurrection Philadelphia, 123 S. 17th St

Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.
May 20

2026 Ride of Silence

6:45 PM · North Apron of City Hall to Art Museum steps

Honor the bicyclists killed or injured on our streets with a ride in complete silence throughout the city. The ride will cover 8 miles at a slow, casual pace and will occur rain or shine.

Weekly Newsletter #22 · April 23, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

📚 NEXT MONTH: LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

Get your tickets before they sell out!

Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM — Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. The event will be kicked off by safe-streets champion Senator Nikil Saval, with Inquirer architecture critic Inga Saffron as emcee. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.
 
Get Your Ticket Today

🕯️ RIDE OF SILENCE

Each year, Philadelphia's bicyclists come together to remember and honor those on bikes who were killed or injured by motorists with a ride around the city in complete silence. Since last year's ride, 13 bicyclists have been killed in the Delaware Valley.

This year's Ride of Silence will happen next month on May 20th. Following a brief ceremony at 6:45pm at the north apron of City Hall, participants will bike at a casual pace around the city ending at the Art Museum steps.

🚏 NEW BUS TERMINAL OPENS NEXT WEEK

Next week, the former Greyhound bus terminal will be reopening as a freshly renovated hub for Philadelphia's intercity bus passengers.

 

Check out this article from the Inquirer for a sneak peek: See inside the new Greyhound Terminal on Filbert Street

Ever since the terminal first closed years ago, we've been fighting for a facility that meets the needs of our city's bus riders so we're very excited for it to open next week!

🥳 SATURDAY: CELEBRATE TRAILS DAY

This Saturday, April 25th, is Celebrate Trails Day!

We have a great network of trails throughout the region--so let's celebrate them!

There will be outdoor community events throughout the city and region at various times throughout the day. Find an event here.

 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Philadelphia Tribune / Philly residents show up to Council Chambers, testify overwhelmingly for mayor’s proposed taxes

Jerrett Johnson of 5th Square, a transit advocacy group, urged the Council to approve a new delivery fee for nonessential products, saying the tax “will allocate funds for public transportation without impacting schools.”

Billy Penn at WHYY / Free, year-round SEPTA passes proposed for all Philly students

The passes work from 5:30 a.m. to 8 p.m. on school days, but are deactivated overnight and on weekends, holidays and over the summer. 

Transit advocate Will Tung held up his daughter’s pass during a City Hall press conference Monday and compared it to Cinderella’s carriage, which “turns into a pumpkin, useless,” at midnight.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! Sign the Bicycle Coalition's petition to legalize parking-protected bike lanes!

 

🚌 KEEP TRANSIT WINS IN THE BUDGET

We worked hard to get Zero Fare, municipal Key Advantage, and increased resources for SEPTA into the Mayor's budget plan--help us keep up the pressure on City Council to make these wins a reality!

  1. Take City Council's city budget survey.
  2. Sign up for a hearing at City Hall
  3. Join a neighborhood budget town hall

📅 EVENTS

Apr 25

Celebrate Trails Day

Various times · Various Locations

Saturday, April 25th is Celebrate Trails Day! Throughout the city and region, there will be outdoor community events to celebrate our great network of trails.
May 14

Life After Cars Book Talk

7:00 PM, doors open 6:30 PM · Resurrection Philadelphia, 123 S. 17th St

Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.
May 20

2026 Ride of Silence

6:45 PM · North Apron of City Hall to Art Museum steps

Honor the bicyclists killed or injured on our streets with a ride in complete silence throughout the city. The ride will cover 8 miles at a slow, casual pace and will occur rain or shine.

📖 WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

🚌 TRANSIT

Billy Penn at WHYY / Free, year-round SEPTA passes proposed for all Philly students

🚲 MOBILITY

makedrivingsuckless.substack.com / SEPTA + Carvana = the Philly car buyback program

NBC10 Philadelphia / Family mourns father of 3 who was struck, killed by hit-and-run driver while riding his bike

💼 JOB OPPORTUNITIES

  • Marketing Intern

item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #21 · April 16, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🚲 LEGALIZE PARKING-PROTECTED BIKE LANES

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal on state roads! The few parking-protected bike lanes that currently exist in our city are only allowed as part of a limited pilot program with PennDOT.

The Bicycle Coalition is fighting to change this: Sign their petition to support legalizing parking-protected bike lanes!

📣 MONDAY: ADVOCACY WORKSHOP

📚 ONE MONTH AWAY: LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

Get your tickets before they sell out!

Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM — Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.

Get Your Ticket Today

🏙️ OPEN STREETS THIS WEEKEND

This Sunday, portions of Walnut and 18th Streets in the Rittenhouse area will be car-free from 10am to 5pm as part of Center City District's West Walnut Open Streets.

Enjoy the beautiful spring weather and see how great our city can be when our streets put people first.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🏘️🚏 SUPPORT HOMES NEAR TRANSIT

Help us advocate for more transit-oriented development in Philadelphia! We're meeting with district councilmembers to talk about adding more stations to the Mayor's Transit Oriented Communities Bill. Fill out this form and we'll loop you in with an organizer leading your district, materials, and talking points for your meeting!

 

🚌 KEEP TRANSIT WINS IN THE BUDGET

We worked hard to get Zero Fare, municipal Key Advantage, and increased resources for SEPTA into the Mayor's budget plan--help us keep up the pressure on City Council to make these wins a reality!

7:00 PM – 9:00 PM · Pen and Pencil, 1522 Latimer St

Every American city is divided by crumbling old highways. Every city is trying to figure out what to do with them. Join Ian Coss, host of the Peabody-Award winning podcast “The Big Dig” – along with special guests – for a live taping about Philadelphia’s own attempts to solve that puzzle, and undo the harms of the past.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #18 — March 26, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #18 · March 26, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🚏 WE WON REAL-TIME BUS SIGNS

SEPTA is FINALLY launching a pilot program to deploy digital real-time arrival displays at selected bus and trolley stops across the system.

Our advocates have been speaking in support of these signs for months at SEPTA board meetings, so we're thrilled to see that our advocacy worked.

Real-time bus information is a basic feature that should be available to everyone waiting for the bus, not just to those with smartphones.

Have ideas about where these signs should go first? SEPTA wants to hear them.

🕯️ SATURDAY: REMEMBERING TEDDY EINSTEIN

This Saturday, the Bicycle Coalition will be hosting a memorial ride and ghost bike dedication for Teddy Einstein, a beloved husband and father of two young children who was killed by a driver while biking on Baltimore Pike.

Groups of cyclists will meet up at 9:45am in West Philadelphia (43rd and Chester) and Swarthmore (Myers and Park Avenue, Swarthmore Train Station) to bike to the scene of the crash at 10am.

There will be a pop-up intersection reconfiguration to demonstrate a safer intersection. At 11am there will be a brief ghost bike dedication ceremony, followed by cyclists biking back to West Philly and Swarthmore.

🏫 SUPPORT BETTER STUDENT TRANSIT ACCESS

We're working with Transit Forward Philadelphia to push for universal student fares and want to hear from students, teachers and family members--share your support for universal student fares here.

👋 WE'RE HIRING! - LAST CHANCE TO APPLY

We're excited to announce that we're hiring a part-time Executive Director! Applications submitted by April 1st will be prioritized.

The Executive Director (ED) serves as the chief executive and strategic leader of 5th Square Advocacy. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the ED is responsible for advancing the organization's mission through strong leadership, financial stewardship, partnership development, and operational excellence.

Know someone who'd be a great fit? Share this opportunity — we're looking for a passionate urbanist leader ready to take on Philadelphia's most important transportation and housing fights.

Apply Here

🏙️ MORE OPEN STREETS

Center City District's West Walnut Open Streets are coming back!

Weekly Newsletter #18 · March 26, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

🚏 WE WON REAL-TIME BUS SIGNS

SEPTA is FINALLY launching a pilot program to deploy digital real-time arrival displays at selected bus and trolley stops across the system.

Our advocates have been speaking in support of these signs for months at SEPTA board meetings, so we're thrilled to see that our advocacy worked.

Real-time bus information is a basic feature that should be available to everyone waiting for the bus, not just to those with smartphones.

Have ideas about where these signs should go first? SEPTA wants to hear them.

🕯️ SATURDAY: REMEMBERING TEDDY EINSTEIN

This Saturday, the Bicycle Coalition will be hosting a memorial ride and ghost bike dedication for Teddy Einstein, a beloved husband and father of two young children who was killed by a driver while biking on Baltimore Pike.

Groups of cyclists will meet up at 9:45am in West Philadelphia (43rd and Chester) and Swarthmore (Myers and Park Avenue, Swarthmore Train Station) to bike to the scene of the crash at 10am.

There will be a pop-up intersection reconfiguration to demonstrate a safer intersection. At 11am there will be a brief ghost bike dedication ceremony, followed by cyclists biking back to West Philly and Swarthmore.

🏫 SUPPORT BETTER STUDENT TRANSIT ACCESS

We're working with Transit Forward Philadelphia to push for universal student fares and want to hear from students, teachers and family members--share your support for universal student fares here.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #16 — March 12, 2026
item.description:
Weekly Newsletter #16 · March 12, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

💳🚍 HUGE TRANSIT WINS!

The Inquirer is reporting that Mayor Parker will be announcing at today's budget address that the Zero Fare Program & SEPTA Key Advantage for city workers both have their funding restored!!

This is in addition with an increase in the City's contribution to SEPTA operating and capital funding.

This is a huge win for riders and a huge win for SEPTA!

With our partner, Transit Forward Philadelphia, we have been fighting for restoration of the Zero Fare Program for low-income Philadelphians, and continued funding for the municipal SEPTA Key Advantage program. These are top-level asks in our city budget priority list, and the focus of Transit Forward Philly's week of action.

We visited multiple councilmembers at last week's advocacy day and our volunteers and organizers participated in a massive rally at City Hall.

Both of these programs saw their funding cut last year, and now they will both be around to benefit tens of thousands of riders! Advocacy WORKS!

We can't get these wins without your help, sign up to become a volunteer -- helping one of our committees -- or help us stay afloat by pitching in a few bucks a month as a member!

BECOME A MEMBER

🚲 POP-UP PROTECTED BIKE LANE

More than a year and a half after Dr. Barbara Friedes was tragically killed by a drunk driver while biking in the Spruce Street bike lane, there is still no concrete protection.

Join Philly Bike Action on March 21st at 9am for a demonstration to show how concrete protected bike lanes would look and function on Spruce and Pine Streets. Coffee and donuts will be provided.

RSVP HERE

🚌 NEW BUS NETWORK UPDATES

SEPTA will be rolling out the first phase of New Bus Network starting this August and they're kicking off another round of outreach events starting with a virtual town hall webinar next Wednesday.

New Bus Network Webinar
Wednesday, March 18, 6:30 PM
Virtual via Teams

And next month, SEPTA will be hosting an open house and public hearing at two separate times on April 15th.

SEPTA Annual Service Plan Open House & Public Hearing
April 15, various times
In person at 1234 Market St, Virtual

11am: open house (in person only)
12pm: public hearing (virtual via Webex or in person)
5pm: open house (in person only)
6pm: public hearing (virtual via Webex or in person)

Read more about the New Bus Network rollout from Audacy: SEPTA will begin phasing in its redesigned bus network this fall

🏙️ PHILADELPHIANS LOVE OPEN STREETS

Center City District recently released a report on their West Walnut Open Streets program and the numbers tell a very clear story: Philadelphians love open streets!

Here's what they found: 10,000 average visitors per event, a 27% increase in pedestrian activity compared to prior-year Sundays, a 38% average increase in sales for participating businesses, and a 26% increase in in-store foot traffic on Open Streets days.

Photo credit: Daniel Paschall

Check out the full report here.

👋 WE'RE HIRING!

We're excited to announce that we're hiring a part-time Executive Director!

The Executive Director (ED) serves as the chief executive and strategic leader of 5th Square Advocacy. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the ED is responsible for advancing the organization's mission through strong leadership, financial stewardship, partnership development, and operational excellence.

Apply Here

Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM — Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.

🎟 MEMBER PRE-SALE — OPEN NOWPre-sale tickets open exclusively for 5th Square Advocacy members. Become a member to get your ticket before the general public.

Become a Member & Get Your Ticket

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Inquirer / Mayor Parker backs legislation to boost housing development around SEPTA stations

The urbanist advocacy group 5th Square says that Parker's bill should be broader. The group called for the elimination of parking minimums near transit, an even larger coverage radius, and for multifamily housing to be allowed on land zoned for single-family homes near stations. "These bills are a welcome step toward more housing near transit, but their scope doesn't quite address our massive housing shortage," said Fae Ehsan, board member with 5th Square Advocacy.

item.content:encoded:
Weekly Newsletter #16 · March 12, 2026

5th Square Advocacy is an urbanist organization of grassroots advocates building a coalition for better transportation, housing, and public space in Philadelphia. Thanks to our growing network of sustaining members for making this work possible.

💳🚍 HUGE TRANSIT WINS!

The Inquirer is reporting that Mayor Parker will be announcing at today's budget address that the Zero Fare Program & SEPTA Key Advantage for city workers both have their funding restored!!

This is in addition with an increase in the City's contribution to SEPTA operating and capital funding.

This is a huge win for riders and a huge win for SEPTA!

With our partner, Transit Forward Philadelphia, we have been fighting for restoration of the Zero Fare Program for low-income Philadelphians, and continued funding for the municipal SEPTA Key Advantage program. These are top-level asks in our city budget priority list, and the focus of Transit Forward Philly's week of action.

We visited multiple councilmembers at last week's advocacy day and our volunteers and organizers participated in a massive rally at City Hall.

Both of these programs saw their funding cut last year, and now they will both be around to benefit tens of thousands of riders! Advocacy WORKS!

We can't get these wins without your help, sign up to become a volunteer -- helping one of our committees -- or help us stay afloat by pitching in a few bucks a month as a member!

BECOME A MEMBER

🚲 POP-UP PROTECTED BIKE LANE

More than a year and a half after Dr. Barbara Friedes was tragically killed by a drunk driver while biking in the Spruce Street bike lane, there is still no concrete protection.

Join Philly Bike Action on March 21st at 9am for a demonstration to show how concrete protected bike lanes would look and function on Spruce and Pine Streets. Coffee and donuts will be provided.

RSVP HERE

🚌 NEW BUS NETWORK UPDATES

SEPTA will be rolling out the first phase of New Bus Network starting this August and they're kicking off another round of outreach events starting with a virtual town hall webinar next Wednesday.

New Bus Network Webinar
Wednesday, March 18, 6:30 PM
Virtual via Teams

And next month, SEPTA will be hosting an open house and public hearing at two separate times on April 15th.

SEPTA Annual Service Plan Open House & Public Hearing
April 15, various times
In person at 1234 Market St, Virtual

11am: open house (in person only)
12pm: public hearing (virtual via Webex or in person)
5pm: open house (in person only)
6pm: public hearing (virtual via Webex or in person)

Read more about the New Bus Network rollout from Audacy: SEPTA will begin phasing in its redesigned bus network this fall

🏙️ PHILADELPHIANS LOVE OPEN STREETS

Center City District recently released a report on their West Walnut Open Streets program and the numbers tell a very clear story: Philadelphians love open streets!

Here's what they found: 10,000 average visitors per event, a 27% increase in pedestrian activity compared to prior-year Sundays, a 38% average increase in sales for participating businesses, and a 26% increase in in-store foot traffic on Open Streets days.

Photo credit: Daniel Paschall

Check out the full report here.

👋 WE'RE HIRING!

We're excited to announce that we're hiring a part-time Executive Director!

The Executive Director (ED) serves as the chief executive and strategic leader of 5th Square Advocacy. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the ED is responsible for advancing the organization's mission through strong leadership, financial stewardship, partnership development, and operational excellence.

Know someone who'd be a great fit? Share this opportunity — we're looking for a passionate urbanist leader ready to take on Philadelphia's most important transportation and housing fights.

Apply Here

📚 LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM — Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcast and authors of Life After Cars. They'll discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can build safer, more livable streets in Philadelphia.

🎟 MEMBER PRE-SALE — OPEN NOWPre-sale tickets open exclusively for 5th Square Advocacy members. Become a member to get your ticket before the general public.

Become a Member & Get Your Ticket

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you to everyone who has already joined as a member! Our members fuel our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia.

BECOME A MEMBER

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Inquirer / Mayor Parker backs legislation to boost housing development around SEPTA stations

The urbanist advocacy group 5th Square says that Parker's bill should be broader. The group called for the elimination of parking minimums near transit, an even larger coverage radius, and for multifamily housing to be allowed on land zoned for single-family homes near stations. "These bills are a welcome step toward more housing near transit, but their scope doesn't quite address our massive housing shortage," said Fae Ehsan, board member with 5th Square Advocacy.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚏 INTERCITY BUS TERMINAL SURVEY

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is planning for a future intercity bus station and they're looking for feedback about three possible locations. We recommend selecting 30th and Arch as your preferred location. Take their survey here. Last chance, survey closes Friday!

🚧 SAFER WEST MARKET ST

Market Street is one of our most dangerous roads. There have been 139 documented crashes just between 38th St and the Schuylkill River from 2020 to 2024. We're calling on city and state leaders to make West Market Street safer.

📅 EVENTS

Mar 12

2026 Vision Zero PHL Conference · Bicycle Coalition of Greater Philadelphia

9:00 AM – 4:00 PM · Temple Student Center South, 1755 N 13th St

"Putting Community First: Revolutionizing Street Safety" — a full day of panels on ending traffic deaths in Philadelphia.
Mar 18

6:30 PM · Virtual via Teams

SEPTA's New Bus Network team will be presenting updates on their plan for a redesigned bus network.

9:00 AM – 12:00 PM · Corner of Spruce and 12th Streets

Join PBA for a fun morning sharing with the community how a concrete protected bike lane would look and function on Spruce and Pine Streets. Coffee and donuts!

2:00 PM – 5:00 PM · Cherry Street Pier, 121 N Columbus Blvd

This free, family-friendly gathering brings together walkers, neighbors, and partners from across the city to celebrate a winter season of exploring Philadelphia with live music from Batala Philly and the West Philadelphia Orchestra Balkan brass band.
Mar 28

Remembering Teddy Einstein — Memorial Ride & Ghost Bike Dedication · Bicycle Coalition

9:45 AM · Clark Park, 43rd and Chester

A memorial ride and ghost bike dedication for Teddy Einstein, a beloved husband and father of two killed while cycling along Baltimore Pike.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #15 — March 5, 2026
item.description:
👋 WE'RE HIRING!

We're excited to announce that we're hiring a part-time Executive Director!

The Executive Director (ED) serves as the chief executive and strategic leader of 5th Square Advocacy. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the ED is responsible for advancing the organization’s mission through strong leadership, financial stewardship, partnership development, and operational excellence. This is a hands-on, high-impact position in a lean, traditionally all-volunteer, organization.

Apply here.

📚 LIFE AFTER CARS BOOK TALK

Announcing our Life After Cars Book Talk!
Thursday, May 14 at 7 PM
Pre-sale opens TODAY to members of 5th Square Advocacy -- Sign up here to become a member and score your ticket!
Spend an evening with Sarah Goodyear and Doug Gordon, hosts of the War on Cars podcasts and authors of Life After Cars. The event will be kicked off by Councilmember Jamie Gauthier and emceed by the Inquirer's Inga Saffron.
The authors will discuss the negative impacts of car-dependency and how we can create safer, more liveable streets in Philadelphia.

💳 TOMORROW: RALLY TO SAVE ZERO FARE

Tomorrow at 10am outside City Hall, rally to save the Zero Fare program!

The next city budget may cut the hugely successful Zero Fare program and SEPTA Key Advantage for City employees.

Our advocates fought hard for these two programs which together provide reduced-fare or fare-free SEPTA access for over 70,000 Philadelphians--don't let them get cut!

Sign Transit Forward Philadelphia's petition calling on the City to keep these vital programs and join their rally this Friday.

🔥 FIRESIDE CHAT RECAP

Thanks for coming to our fireside chat last week!

We had a great discussion with Angela Brooks focusing on Mayor Parker’s HOME initiative and how pro-housing advocates can get involved in Philly's housing movement.

 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

Grid Magazine / The efforts to eradicate traffic deaths in Philadelphia launched in 2016. Ten years in, the City is still far from its goal

Not all of Vision Zero’s barriers emerge from Harrisburg. Many are a symptom of dysfunction right here in Philadelphia, says Will Tung, an organizer with the urbanist group 5th Square Advocacy.

“We’re kind of beholden to the roadway paving schedule here,” he says. “OTIS very much ties Vision Zero improvements with the paving schedule, mostly for budgetary reasons. They don’t want to implement a roadway change and then have it get ripped out for repaving a year or two later.”

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🗳️ Run for Committee Person

Running for committee person is surprisingly easy and impactful! Our sister-org 5th Square PAC is encouraging you to run and is providing a tool kit to help you get elected. Sign up here to receive a toolkit of voter lists, how-to guides, and petition forms.

🚏 Intercity Bus Terminal Survey

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is planning for a future intercity bus station and they're looking for feedback about three possible locations. We recommend selecting 30th and Arch as your preferred location. Take their survey here.

🚧 Safer West Market St

Market Street is one of our most dangerous roads. There have been 139 documented crashes just between 38th St and the Schuylkill River from 2020 to 2024. We're calling on city and state leaders to make West Market Street safer.

☁️ Clean Air for Grays Ferry

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

EVENTS

DVRPC Planning and Funding Transportation Infrastructure Across the Region
Mar 4, 06:00 PM | Virtual via Zoom
Join DVRPC for a webinar that will inform and engage residents in major regional planning and transportation initiatives. It will provide an overview of long-range planning efforts for Update: Connections 2050, explain the Transportation Improvement Program (TIP), how projects are prioritized, and show how residents can provide feedback to help shape planning decisions.

Wednesday Night Rides: Native Plants Seed Bombs
Wednesday, March 4th, 7pm meet, 7:10pm roll | Penn Treaty Park
Join a group ride to sow native plant seeds across our city to restore native species and create habitat for local creatures. They'll be scattering seed bombs on a ride through the Riverwards and North Philly, and then end at The Monkey Club, which is featuring native plants pint glasses designed by local artists.

Save Zero Fare and Key Advantage Rally and Press Conference
March 06, 2026 at 10:00am - 12pm | City Hall - North Side
Join advocates from across Philadelphia to call on Mayor Parker and Councilmembers to fund Zero Fare and Key Advantage in the city budget.

2026 Vision Zero PHL Conference
Thursday, March 12th, 9:00am to 4:00pm | Temple Student Center South, 1755 N 13th St
This year's Vision Zero conference, with the theme "Putting Community First: Revolutionizing Street Safety", invites participants to explore how the physical, social, and economic city converge and what’s possible when community needs and lived experiences guide decisions

Remembering Teddy Einstein -- Memorial Ride & Ghost Bike Dedication
Saturday March 28th 2026 • 9:45 am | Clark Park, 43rd and Chester
Join a memorial ride and ghost bike dedication for Teddy Einstein, a beloved husband and father of two young children who was killed by a driver on the afternoon of December 3rd, while cycling along the Bicyclist Baltimore Pike. 

DSA Job Fair
Sunday, March 29th | Location TBA
Philly DSA will be hosting a socialist job fair which will provide brief educational programming and inform attendees about the pipeline into active workplace organizing campaigns 

WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

  • Billy Penn at WHYY / A judge overturned the Washington Square West historic district designation
  • Inquirer.com / ‘Clothespin building’ is slated to become a hotel and up to 500 apartments after office vacancy crisis tanked the price

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

  • The Philadelphia Citizen / How Not to Plan A Neighborhood
  • Grid Magazine / The city’s illegal dumping problem persists despite decades of efforts to curb it

🚌 TRANSIT

  • Inquirer.com / SEPTA trolleys will use AI cameras to catch drivers breaking no-parking rules in Philly

🚲 MOBILITY

  • Grid Magazine / The efforts to eradicate traffic deaths in Philadelphia launched in 2016. Ten years in, the City is still far from its goal
  • Grid Magazine / Cyclists endure weeks of snow-blocked bike lanes
  • strongtowns.org / What's Standing in the Way of Safer Streets in Philadelphia?
  • Grid Magazine / Making bike lanes safer helps more than just cyclists - Grid Magazine
  • makedrivingsuckless.substack.com / Deputize me Cap’n: why the PPA should delegate enforcement

JOB OPPORTUNITIES

5th Square Advocacy / Executive Director (Part-Time)

Clean Air Council / Communications Director

Bicycle Transit Systems

  • Chief Financial Officer
  • Recruitment Specialist

Bicycle Coalition of Greater Philadelphia

  • Swing Bridge Ambassador
  • Bicycle Coalition Educator

City of Philadelphia

  • School Crossing Guard
  • Manager, Business Development
  • Flood Resilience Specialist
  • Deputy Managing Director, Division
  • Internship (OTIS)

AARP / Community Challenge Grant

America Walks / Walking College

Leadership Philadelphia / CEO

Do you like this newsletter and our advocacy work? 
We need your support to sustain Philly's Urbanist Movement (and get cool perks)
Join us as a member TODAY! 

5th Square Advocacy is a grassroots nonprofit organization driven to advance a vision for a more accessible, sustainable, equitable Philadelphia for all residents.

Donations are not tax deductible.

☁️ Clean Air for Grays Ferry

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

February 26, 6pm to 8pm | Indy Hall, 709 N 2nd St
Join our Housing Committee for a “fireside chat” event with city planner Angela D. Brooks who oversees the H.O.M.E Plan as the City of Philadelphia's Chief Housing and Urban Development Officer, and is Immediate Past President of the American Planning Association (APA).

DVRPC Planning and Funding Transportation Infrastructure Across the Region
Mar 4, 06:00 PM | Virtual via Zoom
Join DVRPC for a webinar that will inform and engage residents in major regional planning and transportation initiatives.
