item.description:
🔥 NEXT WEEK: FIRESIDE CHAT WITH ANGELA BROOKS

Next week on Thursday, February 26th, join our Housing Committee for a "fireside chat” event with city planner Angela D. Brooks who oversees the H.O.M.E Plan as the City of Philadelphia's Chief Housing and Urban Development Officer, and is Immediate Past President of the American Planning Association (APA).

We will be hosting it at Indy Hall and providing hoagies, beer, and seltzers.

RSVP HERE

🚸 SCHOOL ZONE SPEED CAMERAS

Earlier this week, the PPA officially turned on speed cameras in five high-crash school zones throughout the city. Following a 60-day warning period, drivers who speed during school hours will begin to receive tickets.

Thank you to CM Thomas for sponsoring legislation to enable this pilot program! We look forward to seeing these five schools become safer, and we hope to see the program expanded to other schools.

🚏 INTERCITY BUS TERMINAL OPEN HOUSE AND SURVEY

Next Wednesday, the Philadelphia City Planning Commission is hosting a public open house on plans for a permanent, publicly owned intercity bus station, and your voice is needed.

Wednesday, February 25, 2026  from 6:00–8:00 PM
Independence Visitor Center, 599 Market Street

This is our chance to push for a new intercity bus station that treats riders with the dignity they deserve, strengthens our city's transit connections around the region and country, and supports a more equitable Philadelphia for decades to come. Stay in the loop by signing up with our friends at Transit Forward Philadelphia 

CPC is also conducting a survey to help them evaluate three different locations they are currently considering.

🗳️ RUN FOR COMMITTEE PERSON

Our sister-org 5th Square PAC is encouraging you to run for the city's most local political office this spring: Committee Person.

These roles are the "foot soldiers" of Philadelphia’s political parties, and by serving in your voting division, you can help reform the political machine, make ward committees more democratic, and ensure we elect representatives who support urbanist positions.

Starting this week, you can get on the ballot by collecting a few dozen signatures from your neighbors; whether you are ready to run or just want more information, SIGN UP HERE to receive a toolkit of voter lists, how-to guides, and petition forms.

🎰 HORSE RACING OR TRANSIT FUNDING?

At a time when Harrisburg is unable to find money in the budget to fund PA's transit agencies, we still somehow have enough money to give the horse racing industry $200 million every year. And now, House Bill 2071 is seeking to increase that amount.

We oppose sending gambling revenue to subsidize horse racing while public transit systems are being forced to cut services and increase fares around the state.

An anti-horse racing coalition organized a petition calling on the PA legislature to end taxpayer support for horse racing. Sign it here.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚏 Intercity Bus Terminal Survey

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is planning for a future intercity bus station and they're looking for feedback about three possible locations. Take their survey here.

🚧 Safer West Market St

Market Street is one of our most dangerous roads. There have been 139 documented crashes just between 38th St and the Schuylkill River from 2020 to 2024. We're calling on city and state leaders to make West Market Street safer.

☁️ Clean Air for Grays Ferry

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

EVENTS

Wharton-Weitzman Future of Cities Conference
Fri, Feb 20, at 8:30 AM | The Study at University City, 20 S 33rd St
The Future of Cities Conference is a student-led, faculty-advised conference that aims to bring together urban innovators and experts from the public and private sectors to challenge and deepen the discourse around the trends, technologies, and policies transforming the future of our cities

Transit Equity Day: Celebrate Public Transit and Envision the Future!
Feb 21, 12:00 PM | Kensington Corridor Trust, 3400 J Street
Join Transit Forward Philadelphia in person for a day dedicated to celebrating public transit and imagining what’s next! Dive into engaging conversation and activities as they explore ways to make PA's transit safe, sustainable and accessible for everyone.

Intercity Bus Terminal Open House
February 25, 6-8 PM | Independence Visitor Center, 599 Market St
The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is hosting an open house to gather community input on their plans for a permanent home for Philadelphia's intercity bus operations.

Urbanist Fireside Chat with Angela Brooks
February 26, 6pm to 8pm | Indy Hall, 709 N 2nd St
Join our Housing Committee for a “fireside chat” event with city planner Angela D. Brooks who oversees the H.O.M.E Plan as the City of Philadelphia's Chief Housing and Urban Development Officer, and is Immediate Past President of the American Planning Association (APA).

DVRPC Planning and Funding Transportation Infrastructure Across the Region
Mar 4, 06:00 PM | Virtual via Zoom
Join DVRPC for a webinar that will inform and engage residents in major regional planning and transportation initiatives. It will provide an overview of long-range planning efforts for Update: Connections 2050, explain the Transportation Improvement Program (TIP), how projects are prioritized, and show how residents can provide feedback to help shape planning decisions.

2026 Vision Zero PHL Conference
Thursday, March 12th, 9:00am to 4:00pm | Temple Student Center South, 1755 N 13th St
This year's Vision Zero conference, with the theme "Putting Community First: Revolutionizing Street Safety", invites participants to explore how the physical, social, and economic city converge and what’s possible when community needs and lived experiences guide decisions

WHAT WE'RE READING

🏙️ HOUSING & LAND USE

  • Spotlight PA / Shapiro wants PA to be a leader on home construction
  • WHYY / West Philly apartment building will bring 40 affordable units to gentrifying section
  • WHYY / Gov. Shapiro announces $1B housing plan to spur new developments in Pennsylvania

🌳 PUBLIC SPACE

  • WHYY / Center City transformation into more of a residential neighborhood continues

🚌 TRANSIT

  • 6abc.com / Driving into the Future: SEPTA plans long-term shift to zero-emission fleet
  • Philadelphia Business Journal / SEPTA eyes mixed-use development at Langhorne train station

🚲 MOBILITY

  • Green Philly / This snowstorm made one thing clear: Philly needs better ways to get around
  • Inquirer.com / Lincoln Drive and dozens of other Philly roads get $13 million from PennDot
  • Philadelphia Magazine / Hey City Hall — When Are You Going to Clear the Bike Lanes?
  • PhillyVoice / Philly to put up 'No Stopping' signs along bike lanes citywide after receiving $1 million from PennDOT

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #12 — February 11, 2026
item.description:
🗳️ TONIGHT: RUN FOR COMMITTEE PERSON TRAINING

Tonight at 6pm, learn how to run for committee person!

Committee persons play important and influential roles in Philadelphia politics, but the ward system can feel confusing and opaque.

Our sister-org Fifth Square PAC will be co-hosting an in-person training tonight in Center City which will provide a practical guide to Philadelphia's ward system and teach you how to run for committee person.

REGISTER HERE

 

Can't make it tonight? There's a virtual option tomorrow from 6-7pm.

❌ CITY COUNCIL SAYS NO I-95 WIDENING

This past week, City Council passed a resolution opposing PennDOT's plans to expand I-95 throughout South Philly and Center City.

Despite abundant evidence that adding new lanes increases pollution and harms surrounding communities, PennDOT is set on expanding ramps and adding new lanes, even at the cost of destroying youth sports facilities.

We strongly oppose I-95 expansion and we thank CM Squilla and City Council for standing with Philadelphians to protect our city.

Read more about the resolution from Broad and Market.

🔥 FIRESIDE CHAT WITH ANGELA BROOKS

Join our Housing Committee on February 26th for a "fireside chat” event with city planner Angela D. Brooks who oversees the H.O.M.E Plan as the City of Philadelphia's Chief Housing and Urban Development Officer, and is Immediate Past President of the American Planning Association (APA).

🗳️ TONIGHT: RUN FOR COMMITTEE PERSON TRAINING

Tonight at 6pm, learn how to run for committee person!

Committee persons play important and influential roles in Philadelphia politics, but the ward system can feel confusing and opaque.

Our sister-org Fifth Square PAC will be co-hosting an in-person training tonight in Center City which will provide a practical guide to Philadelphia's ward system and teach you how to run for committee person.

REGISTER HERE

 

Can't make it tonight? There's a virtual option tomorrow from 6-7pm.

❌ CITY COUNCIL SAYS NO I-95 WIDENING

This past week, City Council passed a resolution opposing PennDOT's plans to expand I-95 throughout South Philly and Center City.

Despite abundant evidence that adding new lanes increases pollution and harms surrounding communities, PennDOT is set on expanding ramps and adding new lanes, even at the cost of destroying youth sports facilities.

We strongly oppose I-95 expansion and we thank CM Squilla and City Council for standing with Philadelphians to protect our city.

Read more about the resolution from Broad and Market.

🔥 FIRESIDE CHAT WITH ANGELA BROOKS

Join our Housing Committee on February 26th for a "fireside chat” event with city planner Angela D. Brooks who oversees the H.O.M.E Plan as the City of Philadelphia's Chief Housing and Urban Development Officer, and is Immediate Past President of the American Planning Association (APA).

We will be hosting it at Indy Hall and providing hoagies, beer, and seltzers.

RSVP HERE

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. 🚧 Safer West Market St

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

🎉 HAHNEMANN HOME BAN BILL HELD

Good news! Councilmember Young's bill (Bill # 251101) to ban housing on the vacant site of the former Hahnemann Hospital has been held. While this bill has been paused for now, we will closely watch whether it makes it back into committee and will keep our petition signers informed.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #10 — January 28, 2026
item.description:
🚧 SAFER WEST MARKET STREET

Market Street is one of our most dangerous roads.

There have been 139 documented crashes just between 38th St and the Schuylkill River from 2020 to 2024.

SIGN OUR PETITION

 

Together with Philly Bike Action, we're calling on city and state leaders to make West Market Street safer with a series of immediate and long-term changes to reduce speeding and remove unnecessary conflict areas between road users.

PBA is also looking for volunteers to help with flyer distribution and in-person petitioning.

⛔ NO PARKING FOR ICE

We strongly condemn the Philadelphia Parking Authority’s decision to contract with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to provide indoor parking garage space for their vehicles.

In Minneapolis and other cities, the deployment of federal immigration enforcement has led to violent confrontations, chaotic scenes, displacement of families, and even death.

We urge PPA to publicly promise not to sign additional contracts with ICE. See our full statement here.

🚇 HELP FIGHT FOR TRANSIT FUNDING

This Friday, join us and Transit for All PA at Fox Chase Regional Rail Station for a morning of canvassing transit riders followed by a press conference calling on Governor Shapiro to prioritize transit funding in the state budget.

🦺 2026 VISION ZERO CONFERENCE

Save the date for this year's Vision Zero Conference!

The 2026 Vision Zero PHL Conference will be held on March 12th on Temple's campus.

The day-long conference will feature local and nationally-recognized speakers & panelists, with the theme "Putting Community First: Revolutionizing Street Safety"

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚫🏘️ No Hahnemann Home Ban

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital (Bill # 251101). Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.

☁️ Clean Air for Grays Ferry

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

🚉 Support the Transit Access Fund

Transit Forward Philly is fighting for a Transit Access Fund to reduce financial barriers for low-income SEPTA riders. In addition to increasing ridership, the Transit Access Fund would help stabilize SEPTA's finances and protect riders from service cuts. Sign their petition here and share your story in support of it here.

EVENTS

As Governor Shapiro prepares to announce his state budget priorities, SEPTA riders are organizing to show we support long-term, dedicated, and expanded funding for transit.

item.content:encoded:
🚧 SAFER WEST MARKET STREET

Market Street is one of our most dangerous roads.

There have been 139 documented crashes just between 38th St and the Schuylkill River from 2020 to 2024.

SIGN OUR PETITION

 

Together with Philly Bike Action, we're calling on city and state leaders to make West Market Street safer with a series of immediate and long-term changes to reduce speeding and remove unnecessary conflict areas between road users.

PBA is also looking for volunteers to help with flyer distribution and in-person petitioning.

⛔ NO PARKING FOR ICE

We strongly condemn the Philadelphia Parking Authority’s decision to contract with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to provide indoor parking garage space for their vehicles.

In Minneapolis and other cities, the deployment of federal immigration enforcement has led to violent confrontations, chaotic scenes, displacement of families, and even death.

We urge PPA to publicly promise not to sign additional contracts with ICE. See our full statement here.

🚇 HELP FIGHT FOR TRANSIT FUNDING

This Friday, join us and Transit for All PA at Fox Chase Regional Rail Station for a morning of canvassing transit riders followed by a press conference calling on Governor Shapiro to prioritize transit funding in the state budget.

🦺 2026 VISION ZERO CONFERENCE

Save the date for this year's Vision Zero Conference!

The 2026 Vision Zero PHL Conference will be held on March 12th on Temple's campus.

The day-long conference will feature local and nationally-recognized speakers & panelists, with the theme "Putting Community First: Revolutionizing Street Safety"

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚫🏘️ No Hahnemann Home Ban

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital (Bill # 251101). Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.

☁️ Clean Air for Grays Ferry

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

🚉 Support the Transit Access Fund

Transit Forward Philly is fighting for a Transit Access Fund to reduce financial barriers for low-income SEPTA riders. In addition to increasing ridership, the Transit Access Fund would help stabilize SEPTA's finances and protect riders from service cuts. Sign their petition here and share your story in support of it here.

EVENTS

Transit for All PA State Budget Canvass / Press Conference
Friday, January 30, Canvass: 7am, Press conference: 9am | Fox Chase Regional Rail Station
As Governor Shapiro prepares to announce his state budget priorities, SEPTA riders are organizing to show we support long-term, dedicated, and expanded funding for transit.

Transit for All PA State Budget Watch Party
Tuesday, February 3, 11am – 1pm | Virtual or at 30 S 15th St
Join Transit for All PA as they call on Governor Shapiro to lead with a budget that moves Pennsylvanians - with new, dedicated investments in public transportation, housing, healthcare, education, and environmental protection.

How to Run for Committee Person in Philadelphia
Feb 3, 6:00 PM - 7:30 PM | 400 W Chelten Ave
Join Committee of Seventy and Black Leadership Pennsylvania for clear, practical guide to how wards shape local politics and how residents can run for committee person.

Manayunk Canal Towpath Boardwalks Rehabilitation Open House
Wed., February 11th, 6:00 - 7:30 PM | Venice Island Performing Arts Center, 7 Lock St
The City will be hosting an open house on its plans to make the Manayunk Canal Towpath more flood-resistant and improve accessibility

Tiny WPA 10th Anniversary Celebration
Feb 12 from 6pm to 9pm | 3145 West Jefferson Street
Join Tiny WPA for a benefit celebrating their 10th anniversary featuring music, an open bar, delicious bites, and a live auction. Come support their work make Philadelphia's public spaces better.

Philadelphia Western Suburbs Trail Summit
February 7, 8:30am - 12:00pm | 9000 Parkview Drive, Haverford, PA
Head to Haverford for a summit to review progress, identify opportunities to improve walking and biking throughout the western suburbs of Philly, and prioritize and help plan continuing trail connections in our communities.

Wharton-Weitzman Future of Cities Conference
Fri, Feb 20, at 8:30 AM | The Study at University City, 20 S 33rd St
The Future of Cities Conference is a student-led, faculty-advised conference that aims to bring together urban innovators and experts from the public and private sectors to challenge and deepen the discourse around the trends, technologies, and policies transforming the future of our cities

There's a SEPTA board meeting coming up this Thursday at 3pm. We'll be there--will you join us?

We'll be speaking about the status of the New Bus Network, real-time arrival signs, and a dedicated trolley diversion route.

SEPTA board meetings are key chances for riders to push SEPTA leadership for promised system improvements and policies that expand transit access and improve reliability. Public testimony helps to hold SEPTA leadership accountable, and even brief comments can make a difference to how the system functions.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #8 — January 14, 2026
item.description:
🤝 MEETUP TOMORROW

Join us TOMORROW, Thursday, 1/15 at 6pm for our next meetup, an urbanist PowerPoint party!

RSVP NOW

🚏 INTERCITY BUS TERMINAL RETURNING IN MAY

Mayor Parker has officially signed into law a funding plan for the revitalization of Philadelphia's former Greyhound intercity bus terminal -- and we were there!

🚋 TROLLEY TUNNEL REOPENING

After a 2-month closure and impacts to 60,000 riders -- The trolley tunnel is finally open again!

We held a fun and impromptu Welcome Home party with our partners at Transit Forward Philly during Monday's morning rush!

Thank you also to everyone who helped advocate for  speeding up the surface diversion routing for trolley riders. SEPTA and the City have heard our demands and followed through with a few changes to speed up service. We are following up to make sure transit priority measures stay in place for future diversions.

🏘️ HOUSING FOR HAHNEMANN

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital (Bill # 251101). Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.

Fortunately, a developer has secured permits for 361 units on the site with ground-floor commercial, but CM Young's overlay would also ban housing in the surrounding parcels--tell him we want housing for Hahnemann!

SAY NO TO HOMES BAN

🏢 POINT ACCESS BLOCKS

Point access blocks are a great way to increase the supply of housing that's both more affordable and more liveable. These single-stair buildings allow for human-scale urban infill with better floorplans and even improved fire safety.

If you're unfamiliar, AIA Philadelphia put together an interesting guide to the housing typology here.

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

📰 5TH SQUARE IN THE NEWS

The Inquirer: Hahnemann developer secures permits for apartments in advance of Council housing ban

But the tradition of “councilmanic prerogative” would likely guarantee its passage because other Council members are unlikely to vote against a bill that affects only one district.

Nevertheless, the housing and transit advocacy group 5th Square has begun a campaign against the legislation and issued a petition earlier this week calling for its withdrawal. 

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚫🏘️ No Hahnemann Home Ban

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital (Bill # 251101). Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.

☁️ Clean Air for Grays Ferry

CHOP is currently constructing a 7-story, 1,000 space parking garage in Grays Ferry which would bring considerable additional pollution to the neighborhood. CHOP has applied for a "Complex Source" air pollution permit from the City of Philadelphia's Air Management Services (AMS)--you can ask AMS to hold a public hearing about the proposal.

🚉 Support the Transit Access Fund

Transit Forward Philly is fighting for a Transit Access Fund to reduce financial barriers for low-income SEPTA riders. In addition to increasing ridership, the Transit Access Fund would help stabilize SEPTA's finances and protect riders from service cuts. Sign their petition here and share your story in support of it here.

EVENTS

Thursday, January 15th, 6-8pm | Resurrection Church, 123 S 17th St, 2nd Fl
Join us for an evening of community-building + urbanist storytelling! Hear from 5th Square Advocacy members and subject matter experts about a range of topics relevant to our built environment. Pizza, beer, and sodas will be provided.

Join Transit Forward Philadelphia for a transit leadership training. You'll learn how you can rally your community to make transit more affordable, safer, accessible, and fully funded.

Feb 12 from 6pm to 9pm | 3145 West Jefferson Street
Join Tiny WPA for a benefit celebrating their 10th anniversary featuring music, an open bar, delicious bites, and a live auction. Come support their work make Philadelphia's public spaces better.

item.description:
🚫🏘️ NO HAHNEMANN HOME BAN

Philadelphia City Council is considering a bill to ban all homes on the site of the vacant Hahnemann Hospital. (Bill # 251101)

Sign here to ask Councilmember Young to withdraw this bill and support mixed-use development for this site.

YES TO MORE HOMES

 

The site at Broad and Race Streets lies on top of an express subway stop, and benefits from proximity to Center City jobs, shops, and cultural amenities. Since the shuttering of Hahnemann in 2019, the site currently provides little value to Philadelphians or tax dollars to the City, despite its central location.

We support mixed-use development for this site to protect neighbors from rising housing costs, grow transit ridership, and support local workers and businesses.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #5 — December 9, 2025
item.description:
🎉 FRIDAY: HOLIDAY PARTY

This Friday, December 12th, join us for our holiday party and awards ceremony!

Celebrate with other Philadelphia built environment activists, neighborhood and community leaders, architects, planners, builders, and sustainability advocates at the urbanist holiday party of the season!

We will also be presenting awards to the winners of the 2025 Urbanist Awards!

🚋 SPEED UP DIVERTED TROLLEYS

Since mid-November 2025, West Philly Trolleys are diverting to 40th and Market due to overhead wire problems in the tunnel.

These trolleys are frequently stuck in University City traffic, especially on Spruce, 38th, and 40th Streets – delaying over 30,000 daily riders.

There are up to 10 times more trolley riders than cars using these streets!

SIGN HERE to tell the City & SEPTA to prioritize riders during EVERY extended trolley diversion and;

  • Create temporary transitways on Spruce, 38th, and 40th Streets
  • Divert vehicle traffic during rush hours & restrict parking
  • Give traffic-signal priority to SEPTA vehicles
  • Provide shelter and benches for waiting riders, especially at 40th & Market
  • Improve bus frequencies in affected areas

🍽️ SUPPORT OUTDOOR DINING

We love our city's streeteries, but unfortunately extensive red tape makes it difficult and expensive for a restaurant to offer outdoor dining.

You can help change that by coming to City Hall on Thursday, December 11th to speak in support of expanding outdoor dining in Philly.

🏘️ HOME PLAN

We are excited to see the HOME plan put a focus on housing investment and policy change and we have some thoughts to share about how the plan can be made even better.

See here for our full statement, but the highlights are:

  • Create a fast-track for affordable housing permits
  • Loosen restrictions around SROs, ADUs, and smaller infill projects 
  • Encourage transit-oriented communities through zoning reform
  • Create a stronger right for tenants to pursue fair rents and housing improvements
  • Provide housing opportunities in all neighborhoods of the city

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

🎉 FRIDAY: HOLIDAY PARTY

This Friday, December 12th, join us for our holiday party and awards ceremony!

Celebrate with other Philadelphia built environment activists, neighborhood and community leaders, architects, planners, builders, and sustainability advocates at the urbanist holiday party of the season!

We will also be presenting awards to the winners of the 2025 Urbanist Awards!

🚋 SPEED UP DIVERTED TROLLEYS

Since mid-November 2025, West Philly Trolleys are diverting to 40th and Market due to overhead wire problems in the tunnel.

These trolleys are frequently stuck in University City traffic, especially on Spruce, 38th, and 40th Streets – delaying over 30,000 daily riders.

There are up to 10 times more trolley riders than cars using these streets!

SIGN HERE to tell the City & SEPTA to prioritize riders during EVERY extended trolley diversion and;

  • Create temporary transitways on Spruce, 38th, and 40th Streets
  • Divert vehicle traffic during rush hours & restrict parking
  • Give traffic-signal priority to SEPTA vehicles
  • Provide shelter and benches for waiting riders, especially at 40th & Market
  • Improve bus frequencies in affected areas

🍽️ SUPPORT OUTDOOR DINING

We love our city's streeteries, but unfortunately extensive red tape makes it difficult and expensive for a restaurant to offer outdoor dining.

You can help change that by coming to City Hall on Thursday, December 11th to speak in support of expanding outdoor dining in Philly.

🏘️ HOME PLAN

We are excited to see the HOME plan put a focus on housing investment and policy change and we have some thoughts to share about how the plan can be made even better.

See here for our full statement, but the highlights are:

  • Create a fast-track for affordable housing permits
  • Loosen restrictions around SROs, ADUs, and smaller infill projects 
  • Encourage transit-oriented communities through zoning reform
  • Create a stronger right for tenants to pursue fair rents and housing improvements
  • Provide housing opportunities in all neighborhoods of the city

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #3 — November 25, 2025
item.description:
🚉 EMERGENCY SEPTA FUNDING

Yesterday, Governor Shapiro announced an emergency allocation of $220 million to SEPTA for a series of critical repairs to Regional Rail, the trolley tunnel, and Metro.

We applaud this move as a step in the right direction. This represents a real down payment toward keeping the Philadelphia region moving and ensuring that the state’s economic engine continues to strengthen and support the rest of the Commonwealth.

But this cannot be where the work to support public transit in the region ends. SEPTA's operating shortfall remains an urgent concern and without closing that gap through stable, long-term funding, riders will remain at risk of service cuts, reduced frequency, service disruptions, and fare hikes.

We urge Governor Shapiro to follow through on this emergency measure with a long-term commitment that fully secures the future of public transit not just for Philadelphia, but across all of Pennsylvania.

📣 SUPPORT SIDEWALK CAFES AND SAFE STREETS

Come to City Council to comment in SUPPORT of sidewalk cafes and bills for safer streets.

City Council, Streets & Services Committee
Tuesday, December 2nd at 10 AM
Philadelphia City Hall, Room 400

  • 🍽️ #251022 - expanding by-right sidewalk cafes in Northwest, South, and West Philly!
  • 🚲 #251024 - adding the 5th Council district (Logan Square, portions of Rittenhouse Square) to the Center City loading zones bill in response to the Pine-Spruce litigation
  • 🚸 #250982 - changing the directions of LeCount and Bambrey streets near South St, in response to multiple crashes involving turning vehicles and people biking.

RSVP here and we will loop you in with our volunteers attending with talking points and register you for comment with council staff.

🏙️ PHILLY2050 SURVEY

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is looking to hear from you about what you want for the future of the city.

  • Transit-Oriented Housing
  • Dense, Walkable Neighborhoods
  • Expansion of Transit Options, including Trolley Modernization, Reimagining Regional Rail and a Subway for Roosevelt Blvd
  • A Network of Protected Bicycle Lanes
  • Repurposing City-Owned Surface Parking Lots

Give Your Input

🏆 URBANIST AWARDS NOMINATIONS DUE BY SUNDAY

Have a friend or colleague who deserves an award for their contributions to Philadelphia's urbanist movement? Nominate them for our annual urbanist awards!

Nominations are due by Sunday, December 1st at 5pm.

We will be presenting awards to the winners at our holiday party on December 12th. Join us to celebrate with other Philadelphia built environment activists, neighborhood and community leaders, architects, planners, builders, and sustainability advocates at the urbanist holiday party of the season!

Get your tickets today!

📚 BOOK CLUB: WHEN DRIVING IS NOT AN OPTION

Join us next week on Wednesday, December 3rd for a book club discussion of Anna Zivarts’ book When Driving Is Not An Option. Discussion will be co-led by Anna Zivarts (author of the book!), Russell Richie (5th Square Advocacy), and Dave Talone (Philly Bike Action). Cheese pizza will be served for dinner.

Anna Zivarts is a disability justice advocate, a low-vision parent, and the founder of the Week Without Driving. She draws attention to the fact that 1/3rd of Americans do not have a driver’s license and says that our transportation systems must be inclusive of EVERYONE–not just people who drive cars. 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

📰 5TH SQUARE ADVOCACY IN THE NEWS

Inquirer.com / West Philly affordable housing project could finally advance, almost 6 years after it was proposed

“It’s a travesty that one deep-pocketed opponent has been able to block access to housing for over 100 families in my neighborhood for years,” said Will Tung, a neighbor of the project and a volunteer with the urbanist advocacy group 5th Square. “It’s more expensive than ever to rent or buy here, and this project would be a welcome change to its current use as a derelict warehouse.”

item.content:encoded:
🚉 EMERGENCY SEPTA FUNDING

Yesterday, Governor Shapiro announced an emergency allocation of $220 million to SEPTA for a series of critical repairs to Regional Rail, the trolley tunnel, and Metro.

We applaud this move as a step in the right direction. This represents a real down payment toward keeping the Philadelphia region moving and ensuring that the state’s economic engine continues to strengthen and support the rest of the Commonwealth.

But this cannot be where the work to support public transit in the region ends. SEPTA's operating shortfall remains an urgent concern and without closing that gap through stable, long-term funding, riders will remain at risk of service cuts, reduced frequency, service disruptions, and fare hikes.

We urge Governor Shapiro to follow through on this emergency measure with a long-term commitment that fully secures the future of public transit not just for Philadelphia, but across all of Pennsylvania.

📣 SUPPORT SIDEWALK CAFES AND SAFE STREETS

Come to City Council to comment in SUPPORT of sidewalk cafes and bills for safer streets.

City Council, Streets & Services Committee
Tuesday, December 2nd at 10 AM
Philadelphia City Hall, Room 400

  • 🍽️ #251022 - expanding by-right sidewalk cafes in Northwest, South, and West Philly!
  • 🚲 #251024 - adding the 5th Council district (Logan Square, portions of Rittenhouse Square) to the Center City loading zones bill in response to the Pine-Spruce litigation
  • 🚸 #250982 - changing the directions of LeCount and Bambrey streets near South St, in response to multiple crashes involving turning vehicles and people biking.

RSVP here and we will loop you in with our volunteers attending with talking points and register you for comment with council staff.

🏙️ PHILLY2050 SURVEY

The Philadelphia City Planning Commission is looking to hear from you about what you want for the future of the city.

  • Transit-Oriented Housing
  • Dense, Walkable Neighborhoods
  • Expansion of Transit Options, including Trolley Modernization, Reimagining Regional Rail and a Subway for Roosevelt Blvd
  • A Network of Protected Bicycle Lanes
  • Repurposing City-Owned Surface Parking Lots

Give Your Input

🏆 URBANIST AWARDS NOMINATIONS DUE BY SUNDAY

Have a friend or colleague who deserves an award for their contributions to Philadelphia's urbanist movement? Nominate them for our annual urbanist awards!

Nominations are due by Sunday, December 1st at 5pm.

We will be presenting awards to the winners at our holiday party on December 12th. Join us to celebrate with other Philadelphia built environment activists, neighborhood and community leaders, architects, planners, builders, and sustainability advocates at the urbanist holiday party of the season!

Get your tickets today!

📚 BOOK CLUB: WHEN DRIVING IS NOT AN OPTION

Join us next week on Wednesday, December 3rd for a book club discussion of Anna Zivarts’ book When Driving Is Not An Option. Discussion will be co-led by Anna Zivarts (author of the book!), Russell Richie (5th Square Advocacy), and Dave Talone (Philly Bike Action). Cheese pizza will be served for dinner.

Anna Zivarts is a disability justice advocate, a low-vision parent, and the founder of the Week Without Driving. She draws attention to the fact that 1/3rd of Americans do not have a driver’s license and says that our transportation systems must be inclusive of EVERYONE–not just people who drive cars. 

👋 BECOME A MEMBER

Thank you so much to those of you who have already joined 5th Square Advocacy as a member!

Our members support our grassroots work for a more accessible, sustainable, and equitable Philadelphia. Will you join us?

As a reminder, 5th Square Advocacy is a new, separate organization from 5th Square PAC which will focus on election-related activities while 5th Square Advocacy will be the new home for our issue advocacy and legislative efforts going forward. Should you have to choose which organization to support with your membership, we highly recommend choosing 5th Square Advocacy.

📰 5TH SQUARE ADVOCACY IN THE NEWS

Inquirer.com / West Philly affordable housing project could finally advance, almost 6 years after it was proposed

“It’s a travesty that one deep-pocketed opponent has been able to block access to housing for over 100 families in my neighborhood for years,” said Will Tung, a neighbor of the project and a volunteer with the urbanist advocacy group 5th Square. “It’s more expensive than ever to rent or buy here, and this project would be a welcome change to its current use as a derelict warehouse.”

🚨 ACTION ITEMS

🚉 Support the Transit Access Fund

Transit Forward Philly is fighting for a Transit Access Fund to reduce financial barriers for low-income SEPTA riders. In addition to increasing ridership, the Transit Access Fund would help stabilize SEPTA's finances and protect riders from service cuts. Sign their petition here.

🚲 Parking-Protected Bike Lane Petition

Parking-protected bike lanes are a great way to make our bikes lanes safer and lower stress, but they are illegal in PA! The Bicycle Coalition is fighting for their legalization. Sign their petition to show your support for safer bike lanes!

EVENTS

Book Club: When Driving Is Not an Option

Join us, the Bicycle Coalition, and Philly Bike Action for a book club discussion of Anna Zivarts’ book When Driving Is Not An Option. Discussion will be co-led by Anna Zivarts (author of the book!), Russell Richie (5th Square Advocacy), and Dave Talone (Philly Bike Action) with pizza served for dinner.

Join Pro-Housing Philly for their December meeting, featuring guest speakers Senator Nikil Saval and Rep. Tarik Khan. They will discuss the Harrisburg politics of housing reform and talk with the reps about the housing bills they're working on at the state level.

item.title: Weekly Newsletter #2 — November 18, 2025
item.description:
🏙️ A BETTER MARKET EAST

Ask for a more walkable, vibrant and dense Market East.

The City is leading an effort to revitalize Market Street, from Broad Street to the Delaware River -- and is soliciting public input.

Suggested comments:

Traffic & Transportation:

  • Prioritize roadway safety & bus users-- install curb bump-outs, raised & protected bike lanes, and prioritize bus lanes.
  • Remove one eastbound car travel lane to give space to people walking and biking.
  • Discourage curb cuts and parking decks to encourage transit use and preserve walkability.

Vacant property and open space:

  • Prioritize housing units, both affordable and market rate, to provide a stable year-round customer base for area stores and businesses.

Retail and shopping:

  • Promote ground level retail and neighborhood services, with storefronts of varying sizes and doors that open on to the street to enhance safety and walkability.

🚵‍♀️ TOMORROW: SPRING GARDEN CONNECTOR OPEN HOUSE

After years of waiting, the City is finally holding an engagement event for Spring Garden St -- spanning river to river. Attend this Streets Department Open House with us and let the city know you value safety for Spring Garden St!

Sign up on our volunteer opportunities page and we can loop you in with other supporters attending.
